summary: Land node identity Rules A/B/C and the dyadic sampling join in truck-certified as NEW code in kernel/identity.rs (BG-KV2-103-IDENTITY). Rule A certifies equality by equal residuals plus exact componentwise union-hull containment; Rule B transports a certificate across an exact deck translation (two-product-exactness-checked, refusing RefusalKind::NonFinite otherwise) and/or an affine leaf reparameterization with one-ULP-outward (next_down/next_up) interval bounds; Rule C identifies through the shim's typed implication relation against the caller's union certificates. The sec 4.3 dyadic join is a BTreeSet union of prefix-closed address sets with integer-only depth normalization and fixed-order a + (b-a)k/2^d parameter sampling, plus the sec 4.3 shared-edge guard refuse_custom_on_shared (NonDyadicSharedRequest, Disproven). Nine required tests landed green in tests/kernel_identity.rs.

details: 1: no frozen-shape drift - the shim PointCert/IBox2/implication/ResidualId/evidence shapes match the contract quotes in certs.rs/patch.rs/residual.rs/evidence.rs; the module is built entirely on them.

2: no exact-deck-shift premise failure - every period exercised (1.0, 0.5) is exactly representable; the module refuses NonFinite when the two-product residual does not vanish instead of ever rounding.

3: no float comparisons needed for dyadic normalization - address expansion is integer bit work only; the module caps depth at 63 (2^63 fits u64, 2^64 does not) and validates leaves below 2^depth with a ClaimRefuted refusal.

notes: JUDGEMENT (recorded for the reviewer): Rule B's period arguments. The packet's section-1 code block prints rule_b_transport(b: &PointCert, deck: (i32, i32), affine: Option<[[f64; 2]; 2]>), but section-1 prose says the period arrives as dyadic-representable f64 arguments (period_u, period_v) and the section-3 ground truth requires deck (1, 0) with period 1.0 to shift [0.2,0.3] to [1.2,1.3] exactly. The printed 3-argument shape cannot express the period at all, so the module lands the shape rule_b_transport(b, deck: (i32, i32), period: (f64, f64), affine: Option<[[f64;2];2]>) with the period before affine. If the authoritative truck-fork spec keeps the 3-argument form, this is a one-line seam for the C1 wave to resolve.

JUDGEMENT (recorded for the reviewer): affine outward rounding. Section-1 prose is normative for the implementation: each computed bound is pushed outward exactly one ULP via std f64::next_down/next_up (toward_pos/toward_neg do not exist in std; the deck.rs steppers stay private and untouched). The section-3 phrase 'lo is the largest representable <= exact via toward_neg/toward_pos' is honored as outward rounding that contains the exact scaled extent; the test pins the one-boundary-ULP values numerically against the exact extents and asserts containment of the scaled points.

Branch situation: at dispatch this slot's worktree HEAD was the KV2 wave base 5dd0fe4 on a branch still named packet/BG-KV2-101-K0AUDIT (stale name from the prior slot occupant; run_packet records the actual current branch). packet/BG-KV2-103-IDENTITY already exists but is checked out in slot 2's worktree, so git refuses the checkout here. Per PACKET's 'commit on the current branch', the work was committed on the actual current branch at the wave base as fb18b4c.

The identity source audit test (identity_never_uses_distance_or_tolerance) scans kernel/identity.rs with comments stripped and asserts none of dist/distance/hypot/abs/sqrt/tol/eps/epsilon/tolerance/1e appear in code: identity is decided only by exact box containment, the typed implication relation, and integer address arithmetic.

The dyadic join performs no float comparison: depth normalization expands each request's leaves by pure integer bit operations (address k at depth d' to children k*2^(d-d')..(k+1)*2^(d-d')-1), unioning into a BTreeSet (never a HashMap). Depth is capped at 63 because 2^64 does not fit u64; deeper requests or leaves not below 2^depth refuse ClaimRefuted (Disproven).
